economy.summary: Her priorities page says she will fight to make life more affordable, pursue good jobs with fair wages and benefits, and address rising costs in energy, housing, insurance, childcare, and groceries.
economy.short: Fights to make life more affordable; pursues good jobs, lower costs.

education.summary: Says she will work to increase funding for public schools, especially for students with special needs, and to fulfill Pennsylvania's constitutional guarantee of a free and appropriate education for all students.
education.short: Supports increased public school funding, especially for special-needs students.

healthcare.summary: Says she will fight to protect access to health services, vaccines, medicines, and affordable insurance including ACA plans, Medicare, and Medicaid, and supports legislation preventing corporations from acquiring hospitals and then closing or limiting services.
healthcare.short: Supports protecting health access; opposes corporate hospital closures limiting services.

economy.summary: Her campaign site lists among her record that she provided energy-related cost relief for families and employers.
economy.short: Says she provided energy-related cost relief for families and employers.

taxes.summary: Her campaign site says she fought for responsible state budgets that made targeted investments in priorities without raising broad-based taxes.
taxes.short: Supports responsible budgets, targeted investments, without raising broad-based taxes.

education.summary: Her campaign site says she advocated for increased education funding without raising broad-based taxes, expanded career and technical education opportunities, and supported school safety initiatives.
education.short: Advocated increased education funding, expanded CTE, supported school safety.

energy.summary: Her campaign site cites conservation work, saying she brought back $4 million in state grants to help preserve 810 acres of open space and farmland.
energy.short: Cites grants preserving 810 acres of open space and farmland.

guns.summary: Her campaign site describes her as a supporter of first responders, citing $2.8 million she brought back for emergency services; it addresses public safety through emergency-services funding rather than stating a firearms policy.
guns.short: Cites first-responder and emergency-services funding; no stated firearms position.

abortion.summary: In December 2025 she voted against House Bill 1957, a joint resolution proposing a state constitutional amendment providing for personal reproductive liberty, which passed the House 102-101.
abortion.short: Voted against 2025 constitutional amendment for personal reproductive liberty.
